subject: Clarify: non-training guarantee + retention nuances for logs/backups
messages:
From: Elena Barnes <elena@pioneerbank.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: PioneerBank Security Team <security@pioneerbank.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Quick confirm — 'we do not train' + logs & backups retention details

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. PioneerBank's procurement/security team asked two follow-ups we need to capture in the SOW and questionnaire: 1) a plain-language attestation that PioneerBank data will not be used to train any Redwood models or derivatives (including internal research experiments); and 2) a clear description of retention windows for short-lived operational artifacts (debug snapshots, KV cache dumps, broker logs, and scheduled backups). They want to understand whether those artifacts are retained in a way that could be incorporated into modeling or if additional controls are required.

Can you confirm and provide expected retention windows and deletion mechanics? Also attaching our security questionnaire so you can populate the relevant tabs.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Vendor Security — PioneerBank
[attachment: PBK-2026-security-questionnaire.xlsx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Barnes <elena@pioneerbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick confirm — 'we do not train' + logs & backups retention details

Hi Elena — great meeting, and thanks for the clear ask. High-level answers below; happy to put this into a short attestation PDF and the SOW language.

1) Non-training guarantee (plain language):
- Redwood does NOT use customer-production data to train, fine-tune, or evaluate our models for the hosted API, Dedicated, or Private offerings unless there is an explicit written agreement that specifies data ingestion for training. This includes: request/response text, metadata tokens, and derivatives.
- Exception: anonymized aggregate telemetry (service-level metrics) may be used to improve platform reliability; that telemetry is sampled, aggregated across customers, and cannot be associated with individual customer content.

2) Operational artifacts — retention windows & deletion mechanics (default behaviors):
- KV cache snapshots (ephemeral): retained in-memory and flushed to ephemeral storage only for active sessions. If persisted for debugging, snapshots are time-limited and deleted within 72 hours by default unless a customer-authorized snapshot retention is requested.
- Debug snapshots / request traces: retained for up to 30 days for troubleshooting by default. Customers can request immediate deletion for specific traces via support with the trace id.
- Broker logs (ingress/egress): retained for 90 days for observability and billing purposes; logs are indexed and rotated and are not used for model training. Access is role-restricted and audited.
- Scheduled backups (model artifacts, config): backups are retained per the deployment plan (typically 90–180 days). Backups containing customer metadata are encrypted and stored in region; deletion follows the same retention window and is captured in the snapshot lifecycle logs.

3) Controls we can offer for PioneerBank:
- Enable stricter retention windows per artifact class (e.g., reduce debug snapshot retention to 7 days).
- Configure automatic purge hooks tied to your retention policy and generate deletion receipts (tombstone records) when data is removed.
- Enterprise attestation PDF and a checkbox in the SOW to guarantee "no training" unless otherwise agreed.

I'll loop Marcus for the more technical deletion flow and Neha for legal wording for the attestation. I can populate the questionnaire partially and send a draft attestation by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-nontraining-attestation.pdf (draft)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-22T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick confirm — 'we do not train' + logs & backups retention details

Elena, Laura — quick technical clarification to make sure expectations are precise:

- KV caches are not materialized into long-term training stores. The serving runtime maintains KV state per session on GPU/NVM; those are evicted by LRU or session termination. Any persisted cache for debugging is copied to a transient S3-like store encrypted with customer-specific keys and tagged with retention metadata.
- Deletion workflow: when a deletion request is raised (support or API), an orchestration job marks the objects for deletion, triggers secure wipe (overwrite or cryptographic delete depending on storage class), and updates an immutable tombstone record that includes object id, deletion timestamp, and operator id. We retain tombstones for audit (90 days by default) but tombstones do not contain customer content.
- Snapshots/backups that include model weights are immutable and are versioned; we do not merge customer request/response content into model weights or training corpora.

If PioneerBank requires shorter retention than our defaults we can implement custom retention policies scoped to your account and region; this is handled as an enterprise config and we can include it in the SOW.

-Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer, Runtime Safety
